T133: absent is not zero, especially in pesos. whFmtPeso exists for one recorded reason - Number(null) is 0 and finite, so a null amount slips through as a confident 0.00. A filed top-up of PHP300 once rendered as PHP0.00 and a ledger line of unknown value rendered as +0, a sentence saying the entry moved nothing. The helper prints a GAP for absent and still prints 0 for a real zero, because a person can act on 'we do not know' and cannot act on a wrong number. THE FINDINGS: founder-console - the owner's own cockpit - had ZERO adoption and a formatter that was literally Number(n || 0), the bug itself, while the same file carried a note saying a money number frozen at zero 'does not read as by design, it reads as a feed that died'; its GCash top-up row had no null guard at all. marketplace-seller's earnings formatter used Number(n), so an absent figure printed NaN on the dashboard of the person being paid. marketplace's service picker guarded <= 0, which catches null but NOT undefined - Number(undefined) is NaN and NaN <= 0 is FALSE - so an absent rate fell through as NaN to a buyer. All routed through the helper. ★THE GATE'S OWN FIRST RUN FLAGGED FOUR FALSE POSITIVES and they were NOT acted on: a ternary spans lines, so the GUARDED FALLBACK half of `whFmtPeso(n) : '+Number(n||0)` looked hand-rolled because the helper sat on the line above. 'Fixing' those would have damaged correct code whose fallback exists so the page still renders when utils.js has not loaded. It now reads a window and honours an explicit null branch. Scoped to money surfaces by design - a gate policing every peso sign would catch option labels and prose and be switched off.

T166: 'who sees this?' answered where it is WRITTEN. Every write surface makes a person decide how candid to be, and that decision happens at the composer - answering it on a welcome card, a help page or a toast after the fact is answering it too late or to the wrong person. THE FINDING: voice-journal.html had ZERO audience statements while being the platform's MOST private surface - voice_journal_entries carries auth.uid() = auth_uid on read, update AND delete, so nobody else in the hive can reach a single row. The only place a worker was ever told lived on hive.html's join-flow welcome card: seen once, on a different page, at a moment they were not writing anything personal. A privacy guarantee a person cannot see is one they cannot rely on. THE WORDING IS READ OFF THE RLS, NEVER FROM MEMORY, and this trajectory carries the scar - a welcome card written the same week claimed the Voice Journal was the ONLY worker-private surface while the policies said otherwise (skill_profiles, badges and exam_attempts are auth_uid-scoped too). So the gate checks BOTH ENDS: the claim on the page AND the policies in the database, failing if a page claims a privacy the policies do not give - a promise the database does not keep being worse than no promise at all. Deliberately a SHORT NAMED LIST of surfaces where a person commits words others might read, not every input on the platform: a gate demanding an audience label on search boxes and filters would be switched off within a week. Resurrection: RED on the pre-fix voice-journal.

T117 / WCAG 2.5.7: nothing may become reachable ONLY by dragging. A worker in gloves, a person with a tremor and anyone on a trackpad share one need - no function should require a dragging movement. The census found the platform CLEAN, and every gesture it has is harmless: nav-hub and companion-launcher let a person DRAG the floating button out of the way while opening it stays a TAP; session-timeout listens for touchstart as an activity SIGNAL, not a gesture requirement; wh-persona sets draggable=false, disabling dragging rather than requiring it. The one genuine keyboard trap in this family was already closed centrally - .wh-scroll-x regions scrolled by swipe were unreachable from a keyboard (axe scrollable-region-focusable, eight on project-report), fixed where the shared class lives rather than per call site. THE GATE FOUND A HIT ON ITS FIRST RUN and it was checked rather than assumed: integrations.html registers a drop handler for CMMS imports - and it is guarded by if (dropZone && fileInput), with a real labelled input type=file wired to the SAME handleFile on change. Drag-and-drop over a working file picker is exactly what 2.5.7 asks for, so it is justified by name with that reason recorded. A NEW gesture file fails - not because dragging is forbidden, but because 'is there a tap that does the same thing?' is a question somebody must answer out loud before it ships. Scoped to product surfaces: vendor bundles and the measurement tooling whose JOB is to find drag handlers are excluded, since a lens that greps for dragstart would otherwise fail a gate about dragstart. ★MERGED WITH T75 (2026-08-26), which asked the same question of dayplanner and found it has NO drag machinery at all - the walk's premise was wrong, there was no drag to alternate. That pass added the rule that now decides the FAB repositioners: a handler assigning only style.left/right/top/bottom MOVES a control and confers no capability, so it passes, while one that also mutates data (insert, splice, sort_order) is load-bearing and must offer a tap. Deciding by what the handler WRITES rather than by which file it lives in keeps the exemption from becoming a licence. ★AND A REAL MISTAKE WORTH RECORDING: driving T75 I wrote a second version of this gate straight over the T117 file, having read 'updated successfully' as 'created', then removed 102 unrelated gate registrations with an over-greedy cleanup regex. The duplicate-id guard caught the first, a HEAD diff caught and repaired the second. A duplicate id is a signal to MERGE two efforts, never to register the same name twice.

T29: acting on an alert must make the ALERT GO AWAY (2026-08-27). An alert inbox that never empties is an inbox people stop reading, so the chain has to close: the alert names an action, links to where that action is taken, and DOING it removes the alert — with nobody marking anything by hand. ★THE CLOSURE IS STRUCTURAL, WHICH IS THE STRONGEST KIND: alert-hub's PM alerts are DERIVED, not stored — they come from v_pm_scope_items_truth filtered is_overdue=true, so there is no status to update and no second write to forget. Complete the PM and the row simply stops matching. PROVEN LIVE rather than reasoned: inserting a 'done' completion for an overdue scope item inside a transaction takes its overdue count 1 → 0 and moves days_until_due −34 → +7, then rolls back with zero residue. ★TWO ASSERTIONS, because either alone is a half-truth — THE LINK EXISTS (an href to pm-scheduler for the NAMED asset plus an action label; an alert that states a problem and offers no way to it is a notification, not an inbox item) and THE CONDITION CLEARS (a link to a surface that does not actually resolve the alert leaves the loop open while looking closed). ★The gate's own link check was wrong first: a lazy any-character match ending at the first closing brace stopped INSIDE the first nested brace — inside a template expression, well before href and actionLabel — and reported a correctly-linked alert as offering no way to act. Read as a plain forward window now, because that is what the block is.

T11: a deduction that moved NOTHING must not read as success (2026-08-27). Two workers finish repairs on the same part; inventory_deduct locks the item FOR UPDATE so the race is serialised, and the loser's call runs against an empty shelf. ★WHAT THE LOSER GOT, MEASURED LIVE (real item set to 0 inside a rolled-back transaction): `v_qty := GREATEST(0, v_qty - p_qty)` CLAMPS instead of refusing, so asking for 1 with 0 on the shelf returned 0, wrote a ledger row with qty_change 0, changed nothing, and raised NO error. Every caller checked only `error`, so the worker was told 'Entry saved' while their entry claimed a part the shelf never gave up — the shelf and the system disagreeing silently, which is the one thing this trajectory exists to prevent. ★AND THE RETURN VALUE CANNOT TELL THEM APART: it is the new quantity, and 'took the last one' and 'there were none' both end at 0. The LEDGER row can, because it records what MOVED — so callers pass p_txn_id (the function always accepted one) and read that row back through whDeductMoved(); verified under RLS that a member can read their own hive's inventory_transactions row. ★THREE SITES, NOT ONE: logbook's SAVE path, logbook's EDIT path, and inventory's Use modal — and inventory additionally cached `addTransaction(..., -qty, ...)`, recording the amount ASKED, so the page's own transaction list claimed a movement the database never made; it now records what moved. The first version of this GATE had the same disease it was built to catch, grading only the first call it found with re.search while two others kept the defect. ★TEETH (--selftest): the pre-fix error-only shape goes RED, an id passed but never read back goes RED, id+readback+comparison passes, and every live site is asserted green. The DB half rolls back and re-reads the shelf to prove it.

CREDIT SOLVENCY - are the credits given away backed by anything? MARKETPLACE_CREDIT_SUSTAINABILITY §5 named liability cover the number that matters, and §4.5 named spending the float the most dangerous failure mode BECAUSE IT IS INVISIBLE UNTIL IT IS FATAL. Credits enter three ways and they are NOT equal: topup is backed by CASH (a provider paid GCash), cashback is backed by REVENUE (funded out of commission, and the hive_service_settings CHECK already refuses cashback_pct > commission_pct + listing_fee_pct so it cannot outrun the take per transaction), and voucher_grant is backed by NOTHING - platform-funded acquisition minted from thin air. Vouchers are therefore the LIVE GAP: nothing currently bounds them, and a generous promo is indistinguishable from an accident until the float is gone. The invariant held here is `unbacked credits (vouchers) <= credits actually EARNED (commission)` - if the platform has given away more than it has ever earned, it is funding acquisition out of other people's prepayments, which works right up until they spend them. ALSO ASSERTED: a negative CONSUMER balance is impossible by construction (consumers only receive cashback and spend it), so one appearing means credits were spent that were never minted; a negative PROVIDER balance is expected and fine, since commission is debited on completion and min_list_balance is what keeps wallets funded. The arithmetic is a pure function so the self-test proves it catches over-granting and negative consumer balances and passes a healthy ledger WITHOUT needing the real ledger in any particular state - and an empty ledger PASSES vacuously while saying so, rather than reporting a false green. Reads service_credit_ledger via docker exec psql; skips when the DB is down.

PUSH HANDLER CONTRACT — a delivered push must actually reach the person. FOUND 2026-07-30 while dispositioning the test bank's TB-S5-edge-push-delivery-roundtrip cell, whose note read 'nothing proves a real subscription RENDERS the notification'. Checked rather than assumed: the SEND side is well covered (notify-push is VAPID-signed and was proven E2E against the real FCM service) and TWO service-worker validators already exist — validate_sw_offline and validate_sw_shell_membership — but NEITHER mentions push, showNotification or notificationclick even once. The receive side had no gate at all. That gap matters because every failure mode is SILENT, and sw.js says so itself: 'Without these handlers a delivered push silently no-ops.' The push arrives, the worker wakes, nothing appears, and nothing errors anywhere a person or a log would see it — a provider just misses the job. SEVEN invariants, each a silent failure: (1) a `push` listener exists (else the push is delivered and discarded); (2) the handler calls showNotification (else the worker wakes and renders nothing); (3) that call is INSIDE event.waitUntil — brace-matched, and the check requires waitUntil to WRAP it rather than merely appear in the handler, because a bare showNotification works on a warm worker and fails on a cold one, which is the hardest kind of bug to reproduce; (4) e.data.json() is guarded by try/catch, since a non-JSON payload THROWS and one malformed push then silently suppresses the notification; (5) a `notificationclick` listener exists (else the tap does nothing); (6) it focuses a tab or opens one (else the notification is a dead end); (7) it closes the notification (else the tray keeps an item the user already acted on). Static by design — these are properties of the file that ships to installed PWAs, and the CACHE_NAME comment records the cost of getting it wrong: 'without this bump installed PWAs keep the handler-less worker'. WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLAIM: the OS notification tray is outside any harness, so 'the human saw it' stays unprobeable; the runtime tier (dispatch a push event to a registered worker and assert showNotification fired) remains recorded as owed with this gate named as its first half, so the residual gap has a shape instead of a shrug. Self-test proves all 7 hold on the shipped worker AND that five deliberately broken workers are each caught.

P7 double-submit lock gate (static teeth) — every `getElementById('...').addEventListener('click', H)` bound to a WRITE handler H (name submit/save/confirm/create/add/send/publish/approve/reject/delete OR the body issues a `db.from().insert/upsert/update/delete` / `db.rpc` write) MUST be single-flight-locked, EITHER by wrapping the binding in `withButtonLock(this, H)` OR by H disabling its button before the await. A bare unlocked click->write binding = a double-tap fires the write TWICE (PRODUCTION_FIXES #47). REAL bugs locked 2026-07-21: inventory.html submitUse/submitRestock/submitPart (bare -> the non-idempotent inventory_deduct/restock RPC = a DOUBLE stock deduction) now wrapped in withButtonLock; logbook.html submitAsset (bare -> 2nd tap 23505s the (hive_id,tag) unique index) now self-disables. Read-only handlers (all db.from().select) + JS Set/Array .delete()/.update() are excluded (Map.size class). Static/fast. Self-test: --selftest.

DEEPWALK D3 gate (static teeth) — a list render that owns BOTH a first-run empty-state ('No entries yet — log your first X' CTA) AND a search no-results ('nothing matched your filters') must route a 0-result SEARCH to no-results, NEVER to the first-run empty-state. For a SERVER-filtered view (the list var IS the query result => `filtered === entries`) an early `if (entries.length === 0){ show empty-state; return }` fires FIRST and makes the no-results branch DEAD, so a supervisor who searched the whole TEAM feed and got 0 rows sees 'Log your first repair' (a nonsensical CTA). REAL bug found + fixed live 2026-07-22 in logbook.html renderEntries (the length-0 branch is now view-aware: team->no-results, mine->empty-state). Client-filtered views (inventory `filtered = items.filter(...)`) are correct and out of scope. Curated list of server-filtered search views; adding one is a conscious UX decision that must extend the gate. Static/fast. Self-test: --selftest.

DEEPWALK D5 gate (static teeth) — the 'number input's declared min/step/bounds are NOT enforced on the write path' class, across TWO central parsers. (a) QTY: a `<input type=number min=1 step=1>` in a modal that submits via a BUTTON (not a native <form>) never has min/step enforced; a bare `parseFloat()||0` lets 2.5 / 1e-9 through => a fractional/absurd stock deduction (inventory submitUse/submitRestock). (b) PRICE: the marketplace post/edit forms are `novalidate`, so min=0 is unenforced; an unvalidated negative hit the DB price_nonneg CHECK (raw 23514) and an over-precision value hit numeric(14,2) overflow, both cryptic to the seller (marketplace handlePostSubmit / marketplace-seller handleEditSubmit). REAL bugs found+fixed live 2026-07-22. FIX (central, METHOD LAW): window.whParseQty (integer qty) + window.whParsePrice (currency: blank=negotiable, 0=free, 2dp, ₱10M cap) in utils.js; every curated number-write handler adopts the right one. Gate locks: both helpers exist + window-exposed, every handler calls its helper, and none has a bare parseFloat/Number inline read (a naive revert). Static/fast. Self-test: --selftest.

DEEPWALK D2 gate (static teeth) — a NON-idempotent client write (a fresh-id INSERT or a decrement/increment RPC) has no idempotency key, so a refresh-mid-submit then retry creates a DUPLICATE / double effect (the button-lock only stops a same-page double-tap; a refresh spawns a fresh page that bypasses it). REAL, live-confirmed 2026-07-22: logbook addEntry (fresh Date.now() id => dup entry), inventory submitUse (inventory_deduct AGAIN => DOUBLE stock deduction), submitRestock (double restock), marketplace handlePostSubmit (dup listing). FIX (central, METHOD LAW): window.whRecentDuplicate(db, table, matchObj, {windowMs, tsColumn}) in utils.js queries for an identical recent row (tight window + specific match => no false-block; best-effort, never blocks a write on error); each handler calls it BEFORE the write and skips on a hit. Live-verified: retry dedups, different value not matched. Gate locks: the helper exists + window-exposed + every curated non-idempotent write calls it. Static/fast. Self-test: --selftest.

T63/T66: a cadence promise needs a scheduler — cron.job is the oracle (2026-08-26). A page telling a reader something happens 'daily' or 'monthly' is making a claim about a SCHEDULER, settled against the live database rather than against prose. FOUND on integrations.html: 'New SAP work orders then flow in daily' and 'WorkHive polls your CMMS API daily' - measured, 26 cron jobs and not one touching cmms-sync, which runs only when someone presses Sync now. Worse than copy: the Sync Schedule control DEFAULTED to 'Daily', saved sync_freq, and plant-connections rendered that value in its status table - three surfaces agreeing on a cadence nothing runs, while nothing anywhere reads sync_freq. What was REAL stayed (the webhook a CMMS posts to, and the push-back cmms-push-completion fires as each job closes). ★THEN THE SAME DEFECT ON A SECOND PAGE, which is why the scope moved: ph-intelligence.html claimed a monthly rhythm in EIGHT places - 'Published monthly', 'refreshes monthly', 'Reports are generated monthly', and worst 'next monthly refresh due soon', a promise about a future event nothing would deliver - with no cron touching intelligence-report either. Scoping a gate to where a bug was NOTICED rather than where the CLASS lives is the failure this session kept finding in other people's checks. ★AND A SAMPLE IS NOT A CENSUS: the first pass on that page read a slice of visible text, caught four claims and declared it clean; a grep for the word found four more. ★ITS OWN VOCABULARY NEEDED FIXING TWICE - it flagged <option> labels (offering a choice is not promising it runs) and then its own honest disclaimer, so selects and denials are excluded; and it miscounted 26 cron jobs as 51 by splitting multi-line commands. ★SKIPS WITHOUT ITS ORACLE. Teeth: reverting either page alone flags that page's claims while the other stays clean.

T65: a verdict needs a denominator — ai-quality's trust-card oracle (2026-08-26). The Worker Trust card is where an owner decides whether the AI is worth paying for. It turned thumbs into a percentage and then into a VERDICT: HEALTHY in green at 70%+, WATCH in amber, LOW TRUST in red below 50%. FOUND: no sample floor. With a SINGLE rating the card read '100% · HEALTHY' in green, or '0% · LOW TRUST' in red - a confident judgement about the whole AI layer from one tap. The zero case was already handled honestly ('NO DATA') and the raw counts already sat beside the figure, so the gap was narrow and specific: a percentage needs a denominator before it can carry a verdict, and below about five ratings a single tap moves it twenty points or more. The number is still shown - hiding it would be its own dishonesty - but it is not dressed as a verdict until it can support one, and the card says what would make it meaningful. Exercised against the shipped branch: 1 and 4 ratings read TOO FEW RATINGS in grey, 5+ resolve to a real tag, and a genuine 2-up/8-down still lands as LOW TRUST in red. ★THE POINT IS NOT TO HIDE BAD NEWS - the gate also fails if the real verdicts disappear, since a card that never judges is its own failure. ★SAME DISCIPLINE THE RELIABILITY WORKBENCH APPLIES to a Weibull fit with too few failures: say the sample is too small and what would fix it, rather than fitting a curve to three points.

T52: what the Engineer lens SELECTS — the TOOLS-registry content oracle (2026-08-27). The sibling gate asks whether the two switches called Engineer agree with each other; this one answers the question T52's own note left open, whether the nav-hub engineer filter selects the right tools. ★THE INVARIANT WITH TEETH: no tool may be tagged `engineer` WITHOUT also being tagged `supervisor`. That is not tidiness. There is no engineer ROLE here — hive_members.role is CHECK-constrained to worker | supervisor — so `roles: ['engineer']` alone puts a tool in NO role's default spine: reachable only by someone who had already gone into the hub and switched the lens by hand, and invisible to the supervisors who ARE the engineers on this platform. nav-hub.js says so at the line that added supervisor to Eng. Design — 'no separate engineer auth exists (the engineer persona IS supervisors in practice, T52); a supervisor needing a calc could not find Eng. Design here' — and the same reasoning applies to every future tool, with nothing holding it. This is the retired-page class (a live control reachable only through a door most people never open), caught at the registry rather than after someone loses a tool. ★AND THE LANE: T52 established the design-and-reliability set (Eng. Design, Analytics, Asset Hub, Project Manager, Project Report, PH Intelligence); each is asserted to keep its engineer TAG so a tool cannot quietly leave the lens while the lens still calls itself Engineer. Tagging, not visibility: isVisibleInMode also drops every hidden:true tool from EVERY mode, and two of the six are hidden Phase-B pages reached from a parent button, so a visibility check would fail them forever for a reason unrelated to engineers. The lane is a FLOOR, not a ceiling — extra engineer-visible tools are allowed, because whether Reports belongs is a judgement the registry records with a reason, not one a validator should overturn. Teeth (--selftest, 5 cases): an engineer-only tool and a lane member leaving the lens both go RED; a universal tool and an absent tool stay green.

CF: a tappable control must not sit past the floor viewport's edge (T113, 2026-08-27). MEASURED: '← Back to Basic Worker' ran +45px past a 390 viewport on inventory and +35px on logbook, its parent computing overflow:visible — part of a real control simply off-screen on the smallest phone the platform supports. ★WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: the page never SCROLLS horizontally. The navbar is a fixed-height flex row and the document's scrollWidth never grows, so every check asking 'does this page scroll sideways at 390?' — the usual Z2 / WCAG 1.4.10 shape — reads perfectly clean while a button hangs over the edge. Scroll is a SYMPTOM of overflow, not a definition of it, and that gap is what this gate closes. ★AND THE ROOT IS RARELY THE OVERFLOWING ELEMENT: shortening the button changed nothing (it was still at 438 in a 390 box at 101px wide). The row was over-full because a SIBLING would not shrink — a flex item defaults to min-width:auto and refuses to go below its content width — so min-w-0 on the group plus truncate on its long label fixed both pages with the full label intact. The oracle ignores fixed/absolute decoration and anything inside a scrolling or clipping ancestor, so it reports only what a thumb actually cannot reach. Resurrection-proved: removing min-w-0 turns it RED (exit 1, naming the control at +228px), restoring it GREEN. ★THE FLOOR IS 320, NOT 390 (corrected 2026-08-27): the first cut of this gate guarded 390 and called it the floor, but the platform's declared floor is 320 (T113 / WCAG 1.4.10) — 390 is merely the common phone. A gate on the wider box cannot see what only breaks in the narrower one, and moving it found TWO more offenders the same day: community's post action row gives a supervisor viewing their OWN post FIVE icon buttons instead of four, and the fifth — Delete, which also carries a deliberate 22px Z3 gap so a destructive control is never adjacent to a routine one — ran 15px off-screen, so the delete control was unreachable on exactly the posts its owner is most likely to manage; and analytics' 'Stage 3' badge sat 10px past, because .hdr-right is deliberately flex-shrink:0 (its EN/FIL buttons owe 44px on both axes) so the row had nowhere to give. Both fixed by wrapping, which preserves the Z3 separation and the 44px minimums instead of trading them away. --width narrows the run and writes its own report; 320 and 390 both green.

T15/T129 (2026-08-28): a number on the glass counts the WORLD, not the fetch. logbook's machine-history panel read .limit(5) and titled itself `data.length + past repairs on + machineId` - a sentence about the array wearing the clothes of a sentence about the plant. MEASURED: 94 machines in the fixture hold more than five fault_knowledge rows and M-003 holds 77, so the panel announced 5 past repairs on a machine with 77 - and this is the panel a technician consults BEFORE opening equipment. Under-reporting a machine's history to the person deciding how careful to be is the wrong direction to be wrong in. Fixed by fetching the true total (count:'exact', head:true - no rows shipped) and rendering '47 past repairs on M-001 · showing the latest 5', verified live; if the count read fails it falls back to describing the LIST ('Latest 5 repairs') rather than a number it cannot support. ★THE CLASS WAS ALREADY KNOWN HERE, which is why the gate holds the SHAPE: asset-hub hit the identical bug (AH16 - '500 reading(s) in the last 30 days' for an asset with 3,174, under-reporting 6x while every mean and sigma above it came from the same truncated slice) and marketplace solves it a third way by rendering an em-dash when the read was partial. Three surfaces, one property; logbook was the instance nobody had walked. ★DELIBERATELY SCOPED to the two sites where the cap is REACHABLE - founder-console (500 campaigns) and marketplace-admin (100 disputes) share the shape but hold 3 and 0 rows, and gating arithmetic that cannot happen yet is noise. Selftest 5/5; its exact-count negative was vacuous first, because logbook holds THREE such reads and the mutation edited an unrelated query 1,600 lines away.

T123 (2026-08-28): whitespace must never decide whether the system works. People paste - a part number from a Viber message, a username from an email - and every pasted value can carry a leading or trailing space the person cannot see. Where the value is used for IDENTITY or MATCHING, that invisible character decides the outcome: a space on si-username/su-username and sign-in fails with correct credentials; a space in the inventory SEARCH and a part that exists returns nothing, which reads as 'we do not stock it' to someone standing at the shelf; a space in part_number/part_name on WRITE is baked into the record, so the row never matches its own search again; a space on a recipient email and the report bounces. All six are trimmed today and this holds them there. ★THE PROPERTY IS DELIBERATELY NOT 'TRIM EVERYTHING': dayplanner's note and logbook's knowledge field are textareas where a person may indent lines, so leading whitespace is CONTENT, and a gate demanding .trim() on every text field would enforce an opinion about prose and eventually be switched off. ★THE SCAN NEEDED CAREFUL READING, WHICH IS WHY THE SUBJECT LIST IS EXPLICIT: a search for untrimmed values reaching a payload flagged inventory's q and cat, both of which are the remembered-filter SNAPSHOT - restored into the input and re-trimmed at the point of use - so judging by the assignment rather than the use would have filed two defects against correct code. ★AND THE SELFTEST MUTATES COPIES, NEVER DISK: its first version rewrote the real product files and restored them in a finally block, which is one crash or one concurrent board read away from a corrupted source or a voided board. Selftest 7/7, each field mutated independently.

T4 (2026-08-28): a wall that promises to send you back must send you back, and only somewhere safe. An anon or hive-less visitor tapping into Community is bounced to the hive gate, and that bounce used to DROP the destination - so a person who set out for one place arrived somewhere else with no way back and nothing explaining why. Now community stamps hive.html?return=community.html and hive.html renders a 'Continue to Community' banner honouring it. TWO HALVES GATED TOGETHER because they are ONE promise in two files: a stamp nobody reads is a query string, a banner with nothing to read is dead markup, and a fix to either side alone breaks the promise with nothing erroring. ★THE THIRD CLAUSE MATTERS MOST - IT IS A SECURITY PROPERTY HIDING INSIDE A USABILITY FEATURE: ?return= is user-controllable, and the naive implementation (location.href = raw) is an OPEN REDIRECT, a link to our own trusted domain that lands the person on an attacker's page wearing our reputation. The guard must be a strict same-origin FILENAME allow-list, never a blocklist - one rejecting 'http://' and '//' still passes '/\evil.com' and a dozen encodings. Nothing about the feature LOOKS security-sensitive, which is exactly why its shape is locked. Fourth: the label is built with textContent, so a crafted filename cannot inject markup even if the allow-list is ever loosened. Selftest 6/6.

T144 (2026-08-28): acking a plant alert hides it for the WHOLE CREW, and the page must say so. alert-hub's dismissal is HIVE state - the upsert is keyed onConflict: 'hive_id,alert_key', NOT on the actor - so one person marking an alert handled removes it from every teammate's feed. That is deliberate: a plant alert is about a machine, not a personal inbox, and it should stop nagging the crew once somebody has dealt with it. ★IT IS ALSO THE ONE FAILURE MODE THIS PAGE CANNOT AFFORD IF IT HAPPENS SILENTLY - a worker tidying what they believe is their own view can blind the entire crew to a live plant condition - so the scope and the SENTENCE are held as ONE property: the write is hive-keyed; the row still records actor (crew-wide AND anonymous would be far worse than either alone); and the toast says both, 'hidden for your whole hive now, recorded under your name'. The old copy said only 'Alert marked handled', which is true and tells the person nothing about who else just stopped seeing it: a scope this wide is defensible when stated and indefensible when discovered. Also gates convergence - setInterval(loadAll, 60000) so a second tab is not stale forever, and a visibilitychange pause so a phone in a pocket is not polling a plant database with no reader. Selftest 6/6. ★ITS ATTRIBUTION NEGATIVE WAS VACUOUS TWICE: a whole-file search for actor: WORKER_NAME also matched an UNRELATED upsert and two comments, so removing it from every dismissal still passed; and the mutation that fixed that deleted the upsert prefix too, tripping 'no upsert found' while the case was labelled 'losing attribution' - detecting something real and proving nothing about the clause it named. The mutation is now a named helper that removes ONLY the actor field, verified to leave the statement intact.

T9 (2026-08-28): a repair entry and its photo land together or not at all. The logbook is the platform's core write - a worker on a plant floor, one-handed, recording what they just fixed - and attaching a photo is where that write goes wrong on most systems, because a photo normally means a SECOND write (upload the file, then insert the row) and two writes have two ways to half-succeed: an orphaned file with no entry, or an entry claiming evidence it does not have. ★NEITHER IS REACHABLE HERE, BY CONSTRUCTION: logbook.html contains NO storage.from(...).upload() at all - the photo is compressed client-side and carried INLINE as a data URL in logbook.photo (a text column) inside the SAME insert as the entry, so there is no second write to fail. The decoupling T12 had to ARGUE for on voice-journal is free here. That is precisely why it needs a gate rather than a comment: adding an upload to this page would read as an IMPROVEMENT in review ('move photos to storage, keep rows small') and would silently reintroduce a failure class the page currently cannot have. ★THE COUPLING RUNS THE OTHER WAY AND IS THE REAL RISK - one row carries the typed work AND the image, so a big photo makes a big row and a failed insert takes the worker's words with it. Both halves gated: an oversize file is refused BY NAME before compression ('Photo too large (max 20 MB).') so the worker learns the limit instead of watching a save fail, and the image is compressed rather than sent raw. Fourth clause: when the AI vision path fails it must say the entry is UNCHANGED, because an analysis failure is not a save failure and a worker who cannot tell them apart retypes work that was never lost. Selftest 5/5, comment-stripped - this page documents its single-write design thoroughly, which is exactly what would let a prose-reading detector pass a file that had lost it.

T130 (2026-08-28): the longest LEGAL value must not break the form that accepts it. A maxlength tells a person how much they may type and says nothing about whether the layout survives them typing it - a field can advertise 200 characters and blow its container at 180, with nobody knowing until a worker with a long part number meets it on a phone. ★A RESTING SWEEP CANNOT SEE THIS, which is why the prover drives flows open: filling capped fields at rest reached 10 of 66, because the other 56 live inside modals, sheets, composers and wizard steps that do not exist until something is clicked - inventory, logbook, project-manager, community and pm-scheduler each reported ZERO capped fields, not for lack of caps but for lack of an opener. Reporting '66 fields, 0 break' off that run would have been a skipped partition reading as a covered one. The value is a single unbroken run of 'W' on purpose: a cap-length SENTENCE wraps and hides the overflow, while a cap-length part number, serial or URL - what people actually paste - does not. ★TWO OF MY OWN CUTS WENT GREEN OVER NOTHING BEFORE THIS WAS RIGHT. First, measuring geometry without visibility produced 18 'defects' that were one CLOSED feedback drawer (visibility:hidden at x=754 against a 390 viewport) counted once per page. Then, guessing the surface selector as '#part-form, #add-part-modal, form' when the real container is #part-modal reached 0 of inventory's 4 fields and reported ok - a prover that opens the right form and measures the wrong box is indistinguishable from a clean run. So each flow now declares how many fields it EXPECTS and under-reach is a FAILURE, not a quiet zero. 18 capped fields across 7 flows at 390, 0 breaking. Teeth 7/7: every flow with fields goes red when its container is widened, each verified clean=0 first. Read-only - fills, measures, restores; never submits.

T53 (2026-08-28): a person who only READS is never forced to write. Not every account operates the plant - a manager, an owner, a client on a site visit signs in to LOOK, reads, and leaves. That lane had no gate, because every existing journey asserts that an ACTION succeeds, and an action-shaped oracle cannot see this persona's defect: being stopped before reading anything at all. ★THE TRAJECTORY SPLITS AND ONLY HALF IS GATEABLE: whether the exec deserves a different LANDING is a design call and stays Ian's; whether a reader is FORCED INTO A WRITE is observable on arrival and needs no decision. Walks six exec-shaped surfaces signed in, settles, and requires no blocking modal, no body-scroll lock, no sign-in/pick-a-hive wall, no focus stolen into a text input (on a phone that opens a keyboard at someone who came to read), and no page error. ★THE SIXTH CLAUSE IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE, because the other five are all ABSENCES and a BLANK PAGE satisfies every one of them - an all-absence oracle grades a dead page as a perfect reading experience. So it also requires the reader actually got words, counting VISIBLE TEXT rather than figures: T53's own walk twice misread a healthy surface as thin, once by counting characters mid-render and once by counting figures on analytics-report, whose correct state is an instruction with no figures at all. The 220-char floor is deliberately low for exactly that page. Read-only by construction - never clicks, types or submits. 6/6 green at 1280. Teeth 5/5 via --teeth: each clause injected on a real signed-in page and asserted to fire, each checked non-vacuous (the clean page reported 0 first), because a gate locking already-correct behaviour has never been seen to go red and is otherwise a green light of unknown wiring.

CF: an optional API's absence must never hide CONTENT (T119, 2026-08-27). MEASURED by removing the capability an older engine lacks: index.html styled `.reveal { opacity: 0 }` and made those elements visible only when an IntersectionObserver callback added `.visible`, so on an engine without the API the constructor THREW, the rest of that script block never ran, and all 14 .reveal elements stayed invisible permanently - the landing page rendered 525 characters of text where every other page rendered 1146+. ★NOTHING WOULD HAVE REPORTED IT: no failed request, no error state, no blank shell - the page 'loaded fine' and simply never faded its content in, the same shape as a skeleton that never resolves. And the source SAID it was safe; the comment above the observer read 'all browsers', which is an assumption wearing the clothes of a check. ★THE GATE REQUIRES BOTH HALVES, because a guard alone is not enough: skipping the observer while leaving opacity:0 in place would pass a naive 'is it guarded' test and still ship a blank page. So every construction must have a feature check BEFORE it - positionally, since a check that runs after the throw protects nothing - AND the hidden class must have a reveal-everything fallback. Fixed at all five call sites, each failing OPEN: the main reveal shows everything, the stagger reuses its EXISTING reducedMotion branch rather than inventing a second path, the before/after rows are shown outright, and the sticky-CTA and nav-highlight observers (which only ADD behaviour) return early - the nav one was the loudest, constructing an observer PER SECTION. Verified both ways: without the API index renders 1061 chars and nothing throws; with it, .reveal still gains .visible on scroll. Teeth 4/4.

CF: a flow's MESSAGES must speak the language the page is set to (T45, 2026-08-27). MEASURED: with wh_lang=fil, all three core field flows refused in English - logbook 'Please select an asset before saving.', pm-scheduler 'Please enter a task description.', voice-journal 'Write a note first, then send it.' ★WHY 100% FIL COVERAGE MISSED IT: the platform has TWO translation mechanisms and they cover different halves of the screen. data-i + whI18nApply swap STATIC markup at load - 442/442 here, which is where 'FIL is 100%' comes from - but every message the FLOW produces is born AFTER that pass, from showToast(...), which takes a raw string. The only translator that reaches those is _t(en, fil) at the call site. So the resting page was fully Filipino and the WORKING page was not, and no load-time DOM sweep can ever see it, because at load the message does not yet exist. ★THE EN CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES IT A MEASUREMENT: each step runs twice, fil and en, and only an identical multi-word message counts as untranslated - separating 'never translated' from 'same word in both languages'. ★AND AN EMPTY READING IS THE INSTRUMENT, NEVER A PASS: three earlier cuts of this prover scored a resting toast placeholder ('Entry saved.' is markup, not a message), a click that threw 'not visible', and a closed <details> whose hidden children still report layout rects - so the gate now refuses to grade any step it did not demonstrably reach. The steps are REFUSALS on empty required fields, so the walk writes no rows and needs no cleanup, and a refusal is the message a worker can least afford to not understand. Fixed by wrapping 14 call sites across the three flows, incl. a second inline refusal path for the same string. Resurrection-proved: the pre-fix logbook turns it RED (exit 1), the fix GREEN.

CF: a capped list must admit the rest exists (T129, 2026-08-27). A long list has to be capped - the DOM cannot carry two thousand rows and stay usable - so the danger is never the cap itself, it is a SILENT one: rows 1-20 of 548 rendered with nothing on screen admitting the other 528. That reads as 'this is everything', and a supervisor planning against it plans against a fifth of their own history. MEASURED at two volumes, which is what this holds in place: with the hive at 941 rows (314 for the signed-in worker) and again at 1641 (548), rows painted stayed 20 -> 20, DOM nodes 1458 -> 1396, first rows 1125ms -> 1221ms. A 75% growth in the reader's own history cost 96ms and NO dom weight, because the slice is constant - and the load-more wrap was offered rather than hidden, so the remainder was disclosed both times. THE PROPERTY IS THREE-PART because any one alone is not enough: the render must SLICE by a display count (or the page grows with the data), something must INCREASE that count (or the cap is a wall, not a page), and the control must be revealed exactly when more rows exist - toggle('hidden', count >= total). That third part is what makes the cap honest; without it a list can slice, own a hidden button, and still tell the reader nothing. Covers logbook and inventory, the two surfaces long enough to need it; teeth are a synthetic negative per part.

T8: re-authenticating costs one sign-in, not your place (2026-08-26). When a token expires, session-timeout.js sends the worker to index.html?signin=1&return=<where they were>, and index.html validates that value before honouring it - an open-redirect guard, and the right instinct. But the guard's character class did not include characters the platform's OWN pages write into their URLs. ★MEASURED BY ROUND-TRIPPING THE REAL CHAIN (page writes filter -> session-timeout captures -> index re-reads): URLSearchParams.set() encodes a space as '+', and audit-log.html mirrors its filters into the URL including `actor`, which is a worker's NAME - so `audit-log.html?actor=Leandro+Marquez` and `audit-log.html?q=pump+seal` both failed the guard and were dropped IN SILENCE, landing the supervisor on the dashboard. That is T28's exact scenario, someone mid-investigation into who changed what, losing their place to a token refresh with nothing on screen explaining why. ★WHY WIDENING TO + , : IS SAFE, ARGUED NOT ASSUMED: the guard's job is to refuse a scheme, a protocol-relative //, and a foreign absolute path, and its ANCHOR already requires the value to begin with <name>.html or /workhive/ - so those three can only appear AFTER the ? or #, where a colon cannot read as a scheme and a plus is just a space. The gate proves both halves rather than trusting the argument: 8 real destinations survive AND 10 attack shapes (javascript:, //evil.com, https://, ../../, backslash-UNC, index.html@evil.com) are still refused. ★IT EXTRACTS THE REGEX FROM index.html instead of restating it, because a gate holding its own copy proves only that the copy is fine - and it FAILS IF THE THREE GUARDS DISAGREE (sign-in, signup, entry bridge), since a fix reaching one path and not the others is how this class survives. Teeth proven on both: the pre-fix class resurrects the two dropped destinations, and reverting a SINGLE guard is caught as disagreement.

T129/T49: the file that leaves the building must be complete (2026-08-26). A logbook export is what an auditor reads, and it is the one artifact whose incompleteness the reader CANNOT see: a short LIST shows a Load more button, but a CSV carries no total, no window and no hint of omission. ★THE RECORDED INCIDENT: the team-branch export handed over `_teamEntries` - only what the feed had fetched, one 30-row page plus whatever Load more added - while the page said '517 entries'. A supervisor exporting a filtered team view for a DOLE/ISO trail got a file that looked whole. The mine branch had been fixed in an earlier arc; the team branch was the one nobody had walked. ★THREE ASSERTIONS: every exporter reads its OWN set by PAGING (a loop with .range) rather than reusing the render buffer, since an export sourced from a screen buffer inherits that buffer's cap; the paging carries a TOTAL order (sort key AND tiebreak), because a non-total order over a paged read can repeat one row and drop another - a file of the right LENGTH and the wrong CONTENTS, worse than a short one; and the property is NON-VACUOUS, checked against the database (largest hive 1,700 rows against a 30-row page) so it cannot pass on a table too small to fail. ★IT NAMES THE BUFFER IT FORBIDS rather than pattern-matching 'looks like an export', because the bug was one identifier. ★AND ITS FIRST VERSION MADE TWO FALSE ACCUSATIONS: a fixed 4000-character window ran past the function's end, through the next one and into the click handler, so it reported BOTH exporters as reusing the feed buffer when neither does - one hit was a COMMENT describing the old bug, the other the handler's ANNOUNCED fallback (which is correct behaviour: it exports the loaded window and says so in a toast). Bodies are now delimited by matching braces. A window sized to today's code is wrong the day someone documents something. Teeth proven on both the buffer reuse and a missing tiebreak.

T124: the printed page must not be the dark theme (2026-08-26). Plants run on paper - a PM schedule goes on the noticeboard, an audit trail into a folder for DOLE - and this platform is DARK. Printed without rules that is either a black sheet that empties a cartridge or, because most browsers drop backgrounds, pale grey text nobody can read. Neither failure appears anywhere ON SCREEN, which is exactly why it needs a gate: print CSS is invisible until it has already wasted someone's trip to the printer. MEASURED: the three pages a plant demonstrably prints already do this properly - white sheet, #111 text, the reset applied to DESCENDANTS (each card and chip carries its own dark background, so a rule on body alone leaves them), the hub/FAB/toasts/dialogs/buttons hidden, and page-break-inside on cards and table rows. This is a RATCHET over work already done, and the held set may not SHRINK - deleting the rules is not a way to pass. ★ITS FIRST VERSION MANUFACTURED FIVE FINDINGS AND ALL FIVE WERE WRONG, which is the part worth keeping: (1) it treated every @media print block as a claim to be printable, but asset-hub's block says in its own comment that it exists so the rule is 'reachable from document.styleSheets' for a DIFFERENT gate, and the report pages already render as light document panels where a dark-to-light reset would be redundant; (2) it read only the FIRST print block, and analytics-report carries SIX - the first being a one-line rule about a field's min-height - so five pages were graded on whichever rule sorted earliest; (3) its skip-list matched substrings against the ABSOLUTE path, and this project lives under '.../Self-learning Road-Map/...', which contains 'learn' - so it excluded EVERY page and reported '0 printable pages examined' while still failing. Three instrument errors before one true reading. ★AND ITS PASS LINE OVERSTATED until corrected: it claimed all 8 pages met the contract when only 3 are held. Teeth proven on a weakened rule AND on deletion.

T20: a refusal must reach the person who was refused (2026-08-26). A supervisor clearing the approval queue rejects an asset, a part, a change order; the item leaves the queue and their job is done - but the WORKER who submitted it is the one who has to act, and if all they ever see is 'Rejected' they resubmit the same thing, give up, or go and ask in person. A refusal that names no cause is a loop the platform opened and did not close. ★BOTH HALVES ARE ASSERTED because either alone is useless: every path writing status 'rejected' records a REASON in the SAME update (a reason captured later, or optionally, is a reason usually missing), and every surface that knows about the rejected state RENDERS it back (a column written and never read is the write-only class, and the submitter is the only person it was written for). ★IT PAIRS WRITES TO RENDERS BY TABLE, NOT BY PAGE, because the halves deliberately live apart: the supervisor rejects from hive.html and the worker reads the reason on inventory.html - a check demanding both in one file would fail the working design. MEASURED: all three paths already comply (hive's queue for asset_nodes AND inventory_items, asset-hub's own reject, project-manager's change orders), rendered as 'Why: ...', 'Why rejected: ... - fix it and resubmit via Edit', and 'Rejected: ...' - and asset-hub even says 'No reason recorded.' for rows predating the column rather than showing an empty box. Nothing was broken; nothing was guarding it, and a fourth reject path added later would have no reason to know the contract exists. ★ITS OWN FIRST RUN WRONGLY ACCUSED asset-hub, by matching a capitalised 'Rejected' caption when that page branches on `status === 'rejected'` inside a template - the state is a VALUE there, not a caption. Teeth proven on both halves.

T24: a reported post must not vanish on the person who wrote it (2026-08-26). When a teammate reports a post the platform hides it from the hive until a supervisor rules, and the easy way to build that is ONE predicate - hide every flagged post from every worker - which is wrong for exactly one person: the AUTHOR, who wrote something, watched it disappear, and was told nothing. They re-post it or conclude the app is broken, and either way the moderation nobody has done yet has already cost their trust. ★THREE PARTIES, THREE OBLIGATIONS: the author keeps seeing their OWN flagged post (the feed query must EXEMPT their rows, not merely filter flagged=false); the author is TOLD in words what happened, who decides, and that teammates cannot see it meanwhile (a post that reappears unexplained is barely better than one that vanished); and the SUPERVISOR sees the REPORTER'S REASON on the card, because judging a flag without knowing why it was raised means opening the audit log first, and a queue that costs a tab is a queue that waits. ★IT CHECKS THE QUERY PREDICATE, NOT JUST THE BADGE, and that is the half a page-level check would miss entirely: if the row is filtered out server-side the badge is unreachable, so the render can be perfectly correct while the author still never sees their post. MEASURED: all three hold today - the author exemption, the UNDER REVIEW state carrying its explanation, and the reporter's reason inline for the supervisor. Teeth proven on the predicate and on the notice.

SW install survives a lost request (10 cases): install ran cache.addAll(SHELL_FILES), which is ATOMIC - one failed entry rejects, the rejection escapes waitUntil, and the worker goes from `installing` to `redundant`, leaving the person with NO service worker at all (no precache, no offline fallback, no network-first page copy) and nothing anywhere saying so. Found 2026-09-10 by asking a browser whether the worker actually CONTROLS the pages a journey walks: under the prover's own offline-3g emulation it returned `registered:true, state:installing, finalState:REDUNDANT` with sw.js itself never dropped, while the same page with routing but no drops installed normally - so the loss killed it, not the instrumentation. Not merely a stress-test concern: the install survives only if all 65 entries land, so at 1-in-12 that is 0.35%, at an ordinary 1% request loss it is (0.99)^65 = 52% (half of real plant-floor installs failing completely), and at 3% it is 14%. Each entry now gets one retry and a file that still will not come is left out rather than taking the install down with it; verified live afterwards - WITH drops the worker reaches `activated` with 65/65 cached, where before it went redundant with zero. Both directions pinned and mutation-tested four ways: restore the atomic addAll, smuggle an addAll in beside the tolerant path, drop the per-file catch, or precache only a hand-picked few, and each is caught.
